lines.trans: Taste this appetizer, gentlemen.
Listen, this is wonderful caviar!
You can immediately sense that it is natural.
Yes, I only ever ate such caviar in Astrakhan.
In Moscow you rarely encounter such quality.
Yes, delicious, very delicious!
The head chef of this restaurant is a true master.
And the fresh bread goes with it perfectly.
We will definitely order another portion.
I am ready to come here every day.
Pass on our sincere gratitude to the chef.
This evening was a glorious success!

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.en: to be felt, be sensed, be palpable
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be felt'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: You can immediately sense the freshness.
You can immediately sense that it is natural.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'rarely'.

examples.text: Наш шеф очень редко хвалит поваров без серьёзного повода.
examples.trans: Our chef very rarely praises cooks without a serious reason.

examples.text: Такие редкие трюфели редко встречаются даже в лучших ресторанах.
examples.trans: Such rare truffles are rarely found even in the best restaurants.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'gentleman', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('Mr (before a surname)') (formal) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('gentlemen (plural, as an address)') (the plural is irregular: господа) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Gentlemen, I apologise. The money will be there.

meanings.note: красная икра = red (salmon) caviar, чёрная икра = black caviar

examples.text: Мама говорила, что у меня на икру аллергия.
examples.trans: Mum said I'm allergic to caviar.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
regularly, or as a general invitation: приходи!

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'appetizer'.
на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to try', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to try, to attempt') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

meanings.en: executive chef, head of a kitchen
meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'head chef', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The head chef developed a new menu.
She works as an executive chef in Moscow.
The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to listen', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
Secondary conversational sense ('hello (on the phone)') ('Слушаю' = I'm listening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

передать.gloss: to pass on, to hand over

meanings.en: to pass on, to hand over, to give
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pass on', forming an aspectual pair with 'передавать'.

examples.trans: Please pass on my regards to your mum.

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'quality' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There won't be any quality anyway.

examples.text: Товарищ майор, тут всё очень плохо слышно. Качества всё равно не будет.
examples.trans: Comrade Major, you can barely hear anything here. There won't be any quality anyway.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'definitely'.

examples.trans: I'll definitely buy you a tank.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: International borrowing in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), declined as a regular feminine noun meaning 'portion'.

examples.trans: The waiter brought two portions of salad.

examples.text: И ещё две порции трески с миндалём!
examples.trans: And two more portions of cod with almonds!
Fyodor, prepare two portions of shrimp.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: plural хлеба, stressed on the ending
plural хлеба, stressed on the ending

examples.trans: The bread is on the table.

meanings.en: to turn out well, to succeed, to manage (impersonal + dative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'даться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to succeed, to manage', paired with 'удаваться'.

examples.text: Я не поняла, как тебе это удалось.
examples.trans: I didn't understand how you managed that.
And did you manage to find a room?

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'sincere' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: Pass on our sincere gratitude to the chef.

examples.text: Конечно, между нами только крепкая искренняя дружба.
examples.trans: Of course, between us there is only strong sincere friendship.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'fresh', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.en: to meet, to pick up (at a station)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'третить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to meet', forming an aspectual pair with 'встречать'.

examples.text: Меня никто не встретил на вокзале.
examples.trans: Nobody met me at the station.
I will meet you at the entrance.

examples.text: А почему этот серьёзный человек тебя не встретил?
examples.trans: Then why didn't this important man meet you at the station?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

подходить.gloss: to approach, to come up; to suit

meanings.note: очередь подходит = one's turn is coming up
Secondary conversational sense ('to suit, to fit') (это мне подходит = that suits me) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Let's go, our turn in the queue is coming up.
The train is approaching the station.

examples.text: Я к печке подхожу. А он маячит перед глазами!
examples.trans: I walk up to the stove. And it dangles right before my eyes!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'excellently'.
Secondary conversational sense ('great!, excellent!') (as a one-word reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I know this town really well!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'every', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'wonderful' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Какой чудесный и невероятно красивый город!
examples.trans: What a wonderful and incredibly beautiful city!

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'gratitude'.

examples.text: Нет, что вы! Это просто благодарность. Двадцать тысяч.
examples.trans: No, not at all! This is just gratitude. Twenty thousand.
This is just gratitude. Twenty thousand.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
Secondary conversational sense ('party, evening event') (e.g. a school evening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Secondary conversational sense ('present, current') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'natural' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: You can immediately sense that it is natural.

meanings.note: predicative: очень вкусно = it's delicious
Secondary conversational sense ('deliciously') (вкусно готовить = to cook well) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'technician', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Они совсем не похожи на настоящих мастеров.
examples.trans: They look nothing like real technicians.

examples.text: А какие признаки должны быть у мастеров?
examples.trans: And what signs should technicians have?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'glory', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('thank God') (in 'слава богу') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

examples.text: Слава богу! Я пьяных за рулём просто терпеть не могу!
examples.trans: Thank goodness! I simply cannot stand drunk people behind the wheel!
